business_problem: India's digital public services needed to reach citizens across many languages and dialects, but traditional language tools lacked the scalability, real-time performance, and platform integration needed to reduce language barriers and support nationwide digital inclusion.
solution_summary: The Government of India worked with KPMG in India to build a broad multilingual AI platform for citizen-facing digital services. At the core of the implementation is a language AI platform powered by more than 300 AI models that support more than 220 languages. The platform combines translation, speech recognition, and chatbot integration so speech and text from citizens can be processed in native Indian languages and then delivered back through government service channels. KPMG's contribution extended beyond technical delivery into policy frameworks, NLP enablement, and expansion strategy, helping the initiative scale responsibly across services. The result was not a concept deck but an operational stack with more than 15 implemented services and more than 12 reference applications used to test, refine, and extend multilingual service delivery across the public sector.

solution_components.role: Embeds multilingual AI capabilities into conversational government-service workflows.

data_flow: Citizen speech and text requests enter the language AI platform through government digital services, speech recognition converts audio input where needed, AI models perform multilingual processing and translation, and the outputs are returned through translated interfaces and chatbot-enabled service channels.

business_outcome: The initiative reduced language barriers in access to government services and increased digital inclusion at scale by operationalizing multilingual translation, speech recognition, and chatbot capabilities across more than 15 implemented services.

KPMG coupled AI technology delivery with policy frameworks, NLP capability building, and expansion strategy.

source_references.title: Reducing language barriers and increasing inclusion

evidence_quotes: KPMG in India's client leads a government initiative focused on using AI to translate speech and text into multiple native Indian languages to help reduce language barriers in accessing the government's services and increasing digital inclusion at scale.
With support from KPMG in India, a broad-ranging language AI platform was developed, powered by more than 300 AI models and supporting over 220 languages.

Through KPMG in India's strategic guidance on AI-driven technology solutions, policy frameworks and expansion strategies, more than 15 services were implemented such as translation, speech recognition and chatbot integration, supported by more than 12 reference applications for testing and refinement.
Traditional language solutions lacked scalability, real-time performance and platform-integration, further limiting reach and impact.
